title: Friction drum
summary: The friction drum, also called the lion drum, is a drum with a stick fixed through the middle of its skin. A wet cloth drawn along the stick makes the skin rumble with a deep, coughing roar like a lion, and it can also be struck as an ordinary drum.
howToPlay: Four places are lit: Roar high and Roar low on the stick, the Skin, and the Shell.
Rub the place a closing ring marks. The cloth slides along the rod and the drum roars.
Roars last a moment, so leave room for them before the next stroke.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: A friction drum is sounded by rubbing rather than by a blow, so the skin itself does the roaring. It can also be struck like any other drum.
credits: Tradition: the friction drum of Zambia; patterns written for this game
